name: Combined oral contraceptive pill for acne
aka: The pill for acne; COC; Yaz, Ortho Tri-Cyclen, Estrostep, Beyaz
summary: Estrogen-plus-progestin birth control pills that the FDA has cleared for moderate acne in women who also want contraception, reducing breakouts.

name: Phenibut
summary: A Soviet-era GABA-B tranquilizer used as a 'low inhib' aid for social ease and confidence; tolerance and withdrawal are well documented.

name: Cannabis / CBD for sleep
summary: Cannabis and CBD products are used to fall asleep faster, with the aim of waking up better rested and looking fresher.

name: Trazodone / prescription sleep meds
summary: A prescription antidepressant widely used off-label for insomnia, taken by people aiming for steadier sleep and a more rested look.

name: Zolpidem (Ambien)
aka: Ambien, Ambien CR, Stilnox, Edluar, Intermezzo
summary: A prescription sleeping pill that speeds sleep onset, used for steadier sleep and a less tired look; carries a boxed warning for complex sleep behaviors.

name: DSIP (delta sleep-inducing peptide)
summary: A nine-amino-acid research peptide reported in the 1970s to promote deep sleep, used by peptide communities for recovery and a rested look.

name: SSRIs for BDD
summary: Prescription antidepressants used for body dysmorphic disorder to ease obsessive appearance thoughts and support a calmer self-view.

name: Antidepressants / anxiety meds
summary: Prescription drugs for depression and anxiety that some people use to ease social anxiety and low mood, which can hold back confidence and presence.

name: 1-Testosterone (1-Test / dihydroboldenone)
summary: A DHT-derived designer steroid once sold online as a muscle-building supplement; controlled in the US since 2005 and untested in human trials.

name: Methyl-1-testosterone (M1T)
summary: An oral designer androgen once sold in supplements for muscle size; known from animal work and a kidney-injury case report.

name: Methylstenbolone (M-Sten / Hybrid)
summary: An oral designer androgen sold online as a supplement or research chemical for muscle gain; published human material is a case report of liver injury.

name: Methyldienolone (Methyldienolone / M-Dien)
summary: An unmarketed oral 19-nor androgen discussed in bodybuilding circles for muscle; almost nothing is published beyond detection chemistry.

name: Dimethyltrienolone (Dimethyltren / RU-2420)
summary: A never-marketed trenbolone analog reported in animal assays at far above methyltestosterone potency; no human data exist.

name: Metribolone (R1881 / Methyltrienolone)
summary: A lab-standard androgen receptor ligand dropped as a drug for liver toxicity; it also turns up in doping cases and bodybuilding circles.

name: Tetrahydrogestrinone (THG / The Clear)
summary: The 2003 designer steroid built to slip past doping tests, taken by athletes for muscle and performance; never studied in people.

name: Desoxymethyltestosterone (DMT / Madol)
summary: A 1960s oral steroid revived in 2005 as a designer doping agent and supplement ingredient for muscle gain; animal data only.

name: Prostanozol
summary: A designer prohormone steroid once sold in bodybuilding supplements for a stanozolol-like lean-muscle effect; now a US Schedule III substance.

name: Methyldiazinol
summary: A 1965 laboratory DHT-derived steroid with a high reported animal muscle-to-androgen ratio, the basis of its interest for building muscle.

name: Epistane (Epitiostanol-derivative, Havoc)
summary: An oral designer steroid sold as a supplement since about 2009 for a harder, leaner muscular look; case reports link it to liver bile-flow problems.

name: Methoxydienone (Methoxy / 18-methyl)
summary: A nandrolone-family steroid from contraceptive research that turned up as a designer muscle supplement; no human trials exist.

name: Bolandione
summary: A nandrolone prohormone sold over the counter in the US until 2005 for muscle gain; now controlled and known for causing doping-test positives.

name: 19-Nor-4-androstenedione (19-norandrostenedione)
summary: A nandrolone prohormone sold over the counter in the US until 2005 for muscle gain, now mostly a doping-control topic.

name: Trendione
summary: A trenbolone metabolite sold online as a prohormone-type supplement for muscle and a harder look; studied mostly in cattle-manure research.

name: Dienedione
summary: A trenbolone-type prohormone sold as a muscle supplement until it was scheduled in the US in 2010; no human studies exist.

name: 4-Androstenediol (4-AD)
summary: An early-2000s oral testosterone prohormone supplement marketed to raise testosterone and support muscle growth.

name: 1-Androsterone (1-Andro)
summary: A designer DHEA-type prohormone sold online for muscle gain; documented mainly in seizure and doping-detection papers.

name: Adrenosterone (11-keto-androstenedione)
summary: A natural adrenal steroid sold as '11-OXO' for fat loss and a leaner physique, via a proposed cortisol-blocking mechanism.

name: Mebolazine (Dymethazine)
summary: A formerly prescribed oral steroid, a dimer of methasterone, that resurfaced in gray-market supplements for lean mass gains.

name: Mestanolone
summary: An old oral 17-methyl DHT steroid, strongly androgenic and weakly anabolic, discussed for strength and hardness; mostly discontinued.

name: Stenbolone
summary: A DHT-derived anabolic steroid related to drostanolone, discussed for lean muscle and a harder look; known from metabolism studies.

name: Mepitiostane (Thioderon)
summary: Japanese oral prodrug of the antiestrogen steroid epitiostanol, discussed for a drier, leaner look; sold as a breast-cancer and renal-anemia drug.

name: Epitiostanol
summary: Injectable Japanese antiestrogen steroid (Thiodrol) used for breast cancer, discussed for a drier, harder look and limiting gynecomastia.

name: Furazabol
summary: Oral Japanese anabolic steroid, a close cousin of stanozolol, discussed for lean mass and strength; known in the West from the Ben Johnson doping inquiry.

name: Oxabolone cipionate
aka: Oxabolone cypionate, Steranabol Depo, Steranabol Ritardo, FI-5852
summary: Obscure long-acting injectable nandrolone-type steroid once marketed in Europe as Steranabol, mentioned for mass gain.

name: Ethylestrenol (Maxibolin)
summary: Old oral 19-nor anabolic steroid, now veterinary-only, used for lean, low-water mass gains; Wikipedia calls it a very weak muscle-builder.

name: Norethandrolone (Nilevar)
summary: One of the first oral anabolic steroids (1950s), cited in bodybuilding history as a forerunner for mass; liver injury ended most use.

name: Mibolerone (Cheque Drops)
summary: A veterinary oral steroid for dogs that circulates in bodybuilding circles as a very potent pre-workout for strength and aggression.

name: Bolasterone (Finaject)
summary: An oral veterinary steroid that physique users have discussed for mass and strength; published material is mostly anti-doping detection work.

name: Chlorodehydromethyltestosterone (Turinabol / Oral Turinabol)
summary: An oral steroid of East German doping fame that lifters use for lean, dry muscle gain with little water retention.

name: Clostebol (4-chlorotestosterone)
summary: A chlorinated testosterone known from skin creams and doping cases that bodybuilders discuss for lean mass.

name: Danazol
summary: A prescription steroid for endometriosis and angioedema that is mentioned in muscle forums for its weak androgenic effects.

name: Tibolone (Livial)
summary: A menopause drug with weak androgenic activity that some forum users discuss as a mild anabolic.

name: Gestrinone
summary: A weakly androgenic endometriosis steroid, parent of the THG designer steroid, discussed for a leaner, harder look.

name: Testolactone (Teslac)
summary: A discontinued steroidal aromatase inhibitor once used for breast cancer, discussed by bodybuilders for limiting estrogen.

name: Formestane (Lentaron)
summary: An injectable steroidal aromatase inhibitor for breast cancer, discussed in bodybuilding for controlling estrogen.

name: Fadrozole
summary: A nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor used for breast cancer in Japan and in lab research, mentioned as an estrogen blocker.

name: Vorozole
summary: A discontinued third-generation aromatase inhibitor now used as a brain-imaging tracer, occasionally mentioned as an estrogen blocker.

name: Aminoglutethimide (Cytadren)
summary: An old adrenal-steroid and aromatase blocker that bodybuilders used before contests to cut cortisol and estrogen.

name: ATD (1,4,6-androstatrienedione)
summary: A prohormone-era supplement aromatase inhibitor, discussed in muscle circles as a way to limit estrogen conversion.

name: 6-OXO (4-androstene-3,6,17-trione)
summary: A prohormone-era aromatase inhibitor used to limit estrogen; one uncontrolled study showed hormone shifts and no body-composition change.

name: Afimoxifene (4-hydroxytamoxifen)
summary: The active form of tamoxifen, studied as a breast gel in women and discussed by some men for gynecomastia.

name: Raloxifene (Evista)
summary: A prescription SERM approved for women's bone and breast risk, used off-label by men to shrink gynecomastia.

name: Toremifene
summary: A tamoxifen-like SERM approved for breast cancer and used off-label for gynecomastia and post-cycle recovery.

name: Fulvestrant (Faslodex)
summary: An injectable pure antiestrogen used for breast cancer that occasionally comes up in gynecomastia discussions.

name: Bazedoxifene
summary: A menopause and osteoporosis SERM used for bone protection and hot flushes, sometimes researched by men among estrogen modulators.

name: Epristeride
summary: An oral DHT-lowering drug of the finasteride family, sold in China for prostate enlargement and discussed by hair-loss communities for keeping scalp hair.

name: Alfatradiol (Ell-Cranell Alpha)
summary: A weak topical estrogen applied to the scalp, sold in Germany and Latin America to slow pattern hair loss in men and women.

name: Topilutamide (Fluridil)
summary: A scalp-applied antiandrogen sold in the Czech Republic and Slovakia to slow pattern hair loss without oral DHT blockers.

name: Dimethylcurcumin (ASC-J9)
summary: An experimental curcumin-derived anti-androgen cream that breaks down the androgen receptor, aimed at acne and tested in two Phase 2 trials.

name: Drospirenone
summary: A progestin with anti-androgen action in some contraceptive pills, FDA-labelled for moderate acne in women who also want birth control.

name: Dienogest
summary: An antiandrogenic progestin in some contraceptive pills that women are prescribed partly for acne, and used alone for endometriosis.

name: Chlormadinone acetate
summary: An antiandrogenic progestin in some European contraceptive pills prescribed to women for acne and oily skin.

name: Nomegestrol acetate
summary: A mildly antiandrogenic progestin in European contraceptive pills, linked by its pharmacology to calmer, less oily skin.

name: Abiraterone acetate
summary: A prescription prostate-cancer drug that cuts androgen production, raised in anti-androgen discussion as a theoretical route to protecting scalp hair or skin.

name: Nilutamide
summary: A prescription antiandrogen that blocks androgen receptors, the pathway behind pattern hair loss and oily skin.

name: Enzalutamide
summary: A potent prescription androgen receptor blocker for prostate cancer, mentioned among antiandrogens in hair and hormone discussions.

name: Erythromycin (acne)
summary: A prescription antibiotic solution labelled in the US for acne, usually paired with benzoyl peroxide to limit bacterial resistance.

name: Sulfacetamide
summary: A sulfa antibiotic, usually combined with sulfur in prescription lotions and washes for acne, rosacea and seborrheic dermatitis.

name: Nadifloxacin
summary: A topical quinolone antibiotic cream for acne used in Japan, parts of Europe and Asia, but not approved in the US.

name: Azithromycin pulse (acne)
summary: Short intermittent courses of an oral antibiotic prescribed off-label to calm inflamed acne for clearer skin.

name: Aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy
summary: A clinic procedure pairing topical ALA with light, labelled for actinic keratoses and studied for acne and oilier skin.

name: Trichloroacetic acid (TCA peel)
summary: A medium-depth chemical peel done by clinicians to renew skin, smoothing texture and fading pigment and some scars.

name: Corticosteroid injection (Kenalog for cysts)
summary: A clinician-given steroid injection into a single inflamed pimple to shrink swelling and redness quickly.

name: Bumetanide
summary: A potent prescription loop diuretic that appears in gray-market water-pill talk for a drier look; no study has tested it for facial puffiness.

name: Torsemide
summary: A prescription loop diuretic that clears excess water through the kidneys; mentioned in depuffing circles for a leaner, less puffy face.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
summary: A common prescription thiazide diuretic that sheds retained water; some forum users take it daily hoping for a less puffy, more defined face.

name: Chlortalidone
summary: A long-acting thiazide-like diuretic that sheds retained water; it appears in forum lists of water pills for a less puffy face.

name: Indapamide
summary: A thiazide-like diuretic that sheds retained water; occasionally raised for facial puffiness, though its trials concern blood pressure and stroke.

name: Metolazone
summary: A potent thiazide-like diuretic that sheds a lot of retained water; mentioned in water-pill talk for a drier look.

name: Acetazolamide (Diamox)
summary: A carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used for glaucoma, edema and altitude sickness that makes the body shed fluid; some users consider it for facial puffiness.

name: Triamterene
summary: A potassium-sparing diuretic, usually paired with hydrochlorothiazide, that sheds water and sodium; mentioned in water-pill discussions for puffiness.

name: Amiloride
summary: A mild potassium-sparing diuretic added to other water pills; mentioned in water-retention talk for a less puffy face.

name: Eplerenone
summary: A selective aldosterone blocker for heart failure and hypertension, discussed on forums as a costlier spironolactone alternative that can reduce water retention.

name: Tolvaptan
summary: A prescription vasopressin blocker that makes the body excrete free water; raised in depuffing discussion for that effect.

name: Demeclocycline
summary: A tetracycline antibiotic that also makes the kidneys excrete free water; raised in depuffing discussion for a slimmer, less puffy face.

name: Theophylline
summary: A prescription asthma bronchodilator that was first used as a diuretic in 1902; raised in de-puffing discussion for facial water retention.

name: Glycopyrrolate (oral)
summary: A prescription anticholinergic pill used off-label for excessive sweating, helping keep skin and clothes dry.

name: Glycopyrronium tosylate (Qbrexza)
summary: An FDA-approved once-daily underarm wipe that cuts heavy sweating, keeping underarms dry and clothes free of sweat marks.

name: Propantheline
summary: An older prescription anticholinergic tablet that dermatology references list for excessive sweating, keeping skin and clothes drier.

name: Aluminum chloride hexahydrate (Drysol)
summary: A prescription-strength antiperspirant that keeps underarms, hands and feet dry and clothes free of sweat marks; irritation is the main downside.

name: Sofpironium bromide (Sofdra)
summary: A prescription underarm gel approved in Japan (2020) and the US (2024) for heavy sweating, for dry underarms and cleaner clothes.

name: Benzatropine
summary: An anticholinergic prescription drug that relieves tremor, muscle spasms and drug-induced drooling, restoring steadier movement and expression.

name: Zilpaterol (Zilmax)
summary: A beta-agonist cattle feed additive that builds lean beef; it appears in physique talk as a relative of clenbuterol.

name: Ractopamine (Paylean)
summary: A beta-agonist livestock feed additive that builds lean pork and beef; it comes up in physique talk and in anti-doping.

name: Albuterol (Salbutamol)
summary: The standard asthma rescue inhaler that some bodybuilders use during cuts to get leaner while holding onto muscle.

name: Terbutaline
summary: A prescription asthma beta-2 agonist that physique forums group with albuterol and clenbuterol as a possible aid to leanness.

name: Fenoterol
summary: A short-acting beta-2 agonist asthma medicine that some people discuss alongside clenbuterol for fat loss and a leaner look.

name: Mabuterol
summary: A clenbuterol-like beta-2 agonist bronchodilator that is discussed as an alternative for cutting body fat and getting leaner.

name: Isoxsuprine
summary: Isoxsuprine is a beta-agonist vasodilator that people interested in leaner physiques discuss because of its beta-agonist class.

name: Rimonabant (Acomplia)
summary: A prescription weight-loss pill that blocks the CB1 receptor to cut appetite; it produced weight loss in trials but was withdrawn in 2008 over mood effects.

name: Lorcaserin (Belviq)
summary: An FDA-approved prescription weight-loss pill (Belviq) that curbed appetite and modestly outperformed placebo in trials; withdrawn in 2020 over a cancer signal.

name: Fenfluramine / phentermine (Fen-Phen)
summary: A 1990s prescription pairing of two appetite suppressants used for weight loss; withdrawn in 1997 after heart valve damage was linked to it.

name: Dexfenfluramine (Redux)
summary: A 1990s serotonin-acting diet pill that cut appetite for weight loss; pulled from the market in 1997 after heart-valve and lung-pressure harms.

name: Phenylpropanolamine
aka: PPA; norephedrine; Dexatrim and Acutrim ingredient
summary: A former over-the-counter decongestant and diet-pill stimulant that suppressed appetite; removed from the market in the early 2000s after a hemorrhagic stroke link.

name: Obetrol (amphetamine salts)
summary: The 1960s prescription diet pill of amphetamine and methamphetamine salts that suppressed appetite for weight loss, and the ancestor of Adderall.

name: Cetilistat
summary: An orlistat-style fat-blocking pill that lets some dietary fat pass through unabsorbed; phase 2 data show weight loss and it is mainly available in Japan.

name: Plenity (Gelesis100)
summary: A swallowed gel capsule taken before meals that swells in the stomach to promote fullness and modest weight loss.

name: HU6
summary: An experimental slow-release prodrug of the fat-burner DNP that makes the body burn more energy as heat; still in phase 2 trials.

name: UBT251
summary: Investigational once-weekly GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist from China, licensed to Novo Nordisk, aimed at appetite and weight loss; phase 2 data exist.

name: Benzphetamine
summary: A prescription amphetamine-type appetite suppressant that cuts hunger for short-term weight loss; Schedule III and labelled for a few weeks of use.

name: Phendimetrazine
summary: An older prescription stimulant appetite suppressant that cuts hunger for short-term weight loss; controlled and labelled for a few weeks of use.

name: Diethylpropion
summary: An older prescription appetite suppressant that cuts hunger for short-term weight loss; Schedule IV in the US and recommended for withdrawal in the EU.

name: Pioglitazone
summary: A prescription type 2 diabetes drug known to raise subcutaneous fat, which is why it comes up in talk about body-fat distribution.

name: Ulimorelin
summary: An investigational gut-acting ghrelin receptor agonist, tested to speed digestion and feeding, followed by people interested in appetite and weight.

name: Anamorelin
summary: An oral ghrelin-receptor drug that raised lean body mass in cancer cachexia trials; muscle-focused users follow it.

name: Macimorelin
summary: An oral ghrelin-receptor agonist that triggers growth hormone release, approved as a one-time diagnostic test for adult GH deficiency.

name: Capromorelin
summary: An oral ghrelin agonist sold as a pet appetite stimulant that also raises growth hormone; a human older-adult trial showed a small lean-mass gain.

name: Relamorelin
summary: An injected ghrelin analogue developed for diabetic gastroparesis that some group with ghrelin-pathway appetite and muscle compounds.

name: Tabimorelin
summary: An experimental oral growth hormone secretagogue that people discuss as a route to higher GH for a leaner, more muscular body.

name: GHRP-1
summary: An early growth hormone releasing peptide that bodybuilding communities group with GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 to raise GH for muscle and fat loss.

name: Alexamorelin
summary: A hexarelin-related GH secretagogue peptide that appears in growth hormone lists for muscle and fat loss, and is mostly known from anti-doping screening.

name: Dumorelin
summary: A GHRH-receptor peptide related to sermorelin and CJC-1295, discussed for growth hormone release and body composition.

name: Rismorelin
summary: A GHRH-analog peptide in the family used to prompt the body's own growth hormone release for leaner body composition and recovery.

name: Deslorelin
summary: A veterinary GnRH-agonist implant that shifts sex-hormone output; it appears on hormone lists for its effect on puberty-linked growth and looks.

name: Ganirelix
summary: A GnRH-antagonist IVF drug that quickly suppresses LH and FSH, which is why it comes up in hormone-manipulation talk in physique circles.

name: Humanin
summary: A mitochondria-derived peptide studied in cells and animals for cell protection, promoted in longevity circles as a way to stay youthful-looking.

name: Dihexa
summary: An experimental angiotensin IV-derived peptide that nootropic users take for memory and learning, studied in rodents.

name: Selank
summary: A Russian-developed anxiolytic peptide that forum users take for calmer social situations and better focus, supporting a more confident presence.

name: Cerebrolysin
summary: A porcine brain-derived peptide mixture approved for stroke and dementia in many countries, used by forum members as an iqmaxxing nootropic for study performance.

name: FOXO4-DRI
summary: A senolytic research peptide that clears aged senescent cells, followed by longevity-minded people for its potential effect on tissue ageing.

name: Modimelanotide
summary: Alpha-MSH analog in the pigmentation-pathway peptide family, developed for kidney injury.

name: Piracetam
summary: The original racetam nootropic, taken for focus and memory to support study, work and training routines.

name: Aniracetam
summary: A racetam nootropic that people take for calm focus and easier social fluency, supporting a more confident, expressive presence.

name: Oxiracetam
summary: A racetam nootropic used for focus and memory, which users fold into their performance and recovery routines.

name: Pramiracetam
summary: A racetam nootropic taken orally for focus and memory, which people use to support study, work and consistent training.

name: Phenylpiracetam (Phenotropil)
summary: A stimulant-leaning racetam used for energy, motivation and stamina to support training and long working days.

name: Noopept (Omberacetam)
summary: A Russian-developed racetam-like nootropic that people take for memory, focus and mood, with small human studies on cognition.

name: Coluracetam
summary: A racetam developed for Alzheimer's and depression and later sold online as a nootropic for focus and mood.

name: Fasoracetam
summary: A never-marketed racetam studied for ADHD that nootropic users take for focus and attention.

name: Nefiracetam
summary: A Japanese racetam studied for dementia and post-stroke apathy that nootropic users take for memory and drive.

name: Sunifiram
summary: An experimental nootropic that users take for learning and focus, based on animal studies of antiamnesic effects.

name: Unifiram
summary: The parent compound of sunifiram, sold online as a potent nootropic for memory and focus; research is in animals.

name: Modafinil
summary: A prescription wakefulness drug that forum users take to stay alert and productive; some report feeling more sociable.

name: Armodafinil
summary: The longer-acting R-enantiomer of modafinil, prescribed for sleepiness and used by forum members the same way for alertness.

name: Adrafinil
summary: A modafinil prodrug once sold in France for vigilance in older adults, used as an over-the-counter route to the same alertness.

name: Vinpocetine
summary: Periwinkle-derived compound taken for memory and focus; a prescription drug in parts of Europe and a US supplement, with an FDA pregnancy warning.

name: Meclofenoxate (Centrophenoxine)
summary: DMAE-ester nootropic with an anti-aging reputation from 1970s elderly-memory studies and a mouse-lifespan report; no studies on skin.

name: Bromantane
summary: Russian stimulant-anxiolytic taken for motivation and lower stress, which users link to better training drive; human data are small and mostly Russian-language.

name: Glyceryl tris-3-hydroxybutyrate
summary: A ketone triglyceride (3GHB) that releases beta-hydroxybutyrate, discussed as a way to raise ketones for appetite and fat loss.

name: R-1,3-butanediol
summary: A diol the body converts into the ketone beta-hydroxybutyrate, used in ketone supplements for appetite and leanness.

name: Alanyl-glutamine
summary: A stable glutamine dipeptide that lifters consider for recovery and muscle retention; its research is in hospital nutrition.

name: Pyridoxamine
summary: A natural vitamin B6 form used as an AGE inhibitor to limit glycation and keep collagen and skin looking younger.

name: Eutropoflavin (7,8-DHF)
summary: A plant flavone used as a BDNF mimic for mood, drive and recovery, which supports general wellbeing.

name: Ramelteon
summary: A prescription melatonin-receptor drug for falling asleep faster, which users tie to a more rested face and clearer skin.

name: Tasimelteon
summary: A prescription circadian-rhythm drug that aligns the sleep-wake cycle, used by some to chase better sleep and a more rested look.

name: Agomelatine
summary: A melatonin-linked antidepressant sold in Europe, used for better sleep and lower stress that users tie to a fresher face.

name: Hydroxyzine
summary: A sedating prescription antihistamine for anxiety, itch and sleep, used to get more rested nights and calmer skin.

name: Low-dose doxepin (Silenor)
summary: A prescription low-dose tricyclic approved for staying asleep through the night, used for more rested, fresher-looking mornings.

name: Suvorexant
summary: A prescription orexin-blocking sleep drug that helps you fall and stay asleep, used for a more rested, fresher-looking face.

name: Lemborexant
summary: A prescription orexin-blocking sleep drug (Dayvigo) for falling and staying asleep, used for a more rested, fresher-looking face.

name: Daridorexant
summary: A prescription orexin-blocking sleep medicine (Quviviq) that people connect with deeper sleep and a more rested-looking face.

name: Eszopiclone
summary: A prescription Z-drug sleeping pill (Lunesta) used for insomnia; people link longer sleep with clearer skin and a more rested face.

name: Zaleplon
summary: A short-acting prescription Z-drug (Sonata) for falling asleep; people link better sleep with clearer skin and a rested face.

name: Zopiclone
summary: A prescription Z-drug sleeping pill (Imovane) used outside the US for insomnia; people link better sleep with a fresher, rested look.

name: Temazepam
summary: A prescription benzodiazepine sleeping pill for short-term insomnia; people link better sleep with clearer skin and a rested face.

name: Gabapentin
summary: A prescription nerve-pain and seizure drug that some people take off-label for sleep, with the aim of a more rested look.

name: Pregabalin
summary: A prescription nerve-pain drug (Lyrica) that forum users take to feel less inhibited and come across as more relaxed in social situations.

name: Mirtazapine
summary: A sedating, appetite-boosting prescription antidepressant used off-label for sleep and weight gain, helping a fuller physique and rested face.

name: Sodium oxybate (GHB)
summary: A tightly controlled prescription form of GHB for narcolepsy that deepens slow-wave sleep, which recovery-minded people link to a rested look.

name: Prazosin
summary: A blood-pressure alpha-blocker used off-label for trauma-related nightmares, with the aim of uninterrupted sleep and a more rested face.

name: Clonidine
summary: A blood-pressure and ADHD prescription drug that appears in forum stress stacks aimed at calmer nights and a more rested look.

name: Zuranolone
summary: A prescription oral neurosteroid for postpartum depression, discussed in mood and sleep recovery circles; carries a driving-impairment boxed warning.

name: Allopregnanolone
summary: A natural progesterone-derived calming neurosteroid behind the postpartum-depression drug brexanolone, discussed for stress relief and rest.

name: Propranolol
summary: A prescription beta blocker used for performance anxiety, with a forum theory about bone growth and face structure.

name: Tianeptine
summary: A French antidepressant with opioid-receptor activity that appears in gray-market mood and stress stacks.
